label: L=9 copy step outputting orig token 2 (input = orig token 1), favoring e/s/h/r
explanation: Very sparse, weak unit (max activation 0.006). Fires only in the copy phase, never during original input or at <DEL>. 97% of mass is in length-9 sequences, and 89% at t=11 (recall_idx=2, two steps after <DEL>, where the input is the fed-back orig token 1). Small tails: recall_idx=1 (t=10) and the last copy steps of L=9 (recall_idx 7-8). The input token matters: e (37% of mass), s, h, r, then w/x; it always fires on a non-first occurrence of that token. The position-only predicate (L==9 & recall_idx==2) covers 86% of mass but has only ~2% precision. Adding the e/s/h/r input filter brings dev precision to 0.11, recall to 0.68 and mass recall to 0.72. Which of these position+token steps actually fire was not explained by first_tok, prev_tok or next_out, so it is likely set by a finer combination of the stored tokens. Magnitude was not checked beyond these breakdowns.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+3.90), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.06), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+2.95), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+2.80), in_tok=e (+1.98), phase=2 & out_tok=h (+1.84). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.67), orig7=- (-2.16), orig4=m (-1.87), orig2=j (-1.85).
